sentences.text: Mesetasaurus is known from two well-preserved tail vertebrae.
The fossils were discovered in the 1980s.
The species was formally described in 2026.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of two tail vertebrae, likely the third and sixth in the series.
The generic name Mesetasaurus refers to the fossil locality, Meseta de Artigas.
The specific name protector honors the Uruguayan hero José Gervasio Artigas.
Mesetasaurus is classified as an aeolosaurin titanosaurian sauropod.
It belongs to the clade Aeolosaurini.
Phylogenetic analysis places Mesetasaurus deeply nested within the clade Aeolosaurini.
Mesetasaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous, potentially from the Coniacian to the Maastrichtian, in what is now Uruguay.
The presence of Mesetasaurus supports a Coniacian to Maastrichtian age for the Guichón Formation.
The discovery of dinosaur eggshells similar to Sphaerovum led researchers to favor a Late Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation.
Some researchers have historically debated a Lower Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation based on similarities with the Migues Formation.
